# Official BIRD structure layer: student_club

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name
- event_date text — The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; values: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00
- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

# Foreign-key relationships
- attendance.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- attendance.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- budget.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- expense.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id
- income.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- member.zip -> zip_code.zip_code
- member.link_to_major -> major.major_id

- aCL IgG real — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgG) concentration
- aCL IgM real — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgM) concentration

- ANA Pattern text — pattern observed in the sheet of ANA examination
- aCL IgA integer — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgA) concentration
- Diagnosis text — disease names
- KCT text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative
- RVVT text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative
- LAC text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative

- Thrombosis integer — degree of thrombosis; values: 0: negative (no thrombosis)1: positive (the most severe one)2: positive (severe)3: positive (mild)

- ID integer — identification of the patient

- Diagnosis text — disease names

- HCT real — Hematoclit; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 29 < N < 52
- PLT integer — platelet; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 100 < N < 400
- PT real — prothrombin time; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 14
- APTT integer — activated partial prothrombin time; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 45
- FG real — fibrinogen; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 150 < N < 450
- PIC integer
- TAT integer
- TAT2 integer
- U-PRO text — proteinuria; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 0 < N < 30
- IGG integer — Ig G; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 900 < N < 2000
- IGA integer — Ig A; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 80 < N < 500
- IGM integer — Ig M; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 40 < N < 400
- CRP text — C-reactive protein; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N= -, +-, or N < 1.0
- RA text — Rhuematoid Factor; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N= -, +-
- RF text — RAHA; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 20
- C3 integer — complement 3; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N > 35
- C4 integer — complement 4; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N > 10
- RNP text — anti-ribonuclear protein; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N= -, +-
- SM text — anti-SM; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N= -, +-
- SC170 text — anti-scl70; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N= -, +-
- SSA text — anti-SSA; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N= -, +-
- SSB text — anti-SSB; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N= -, +-
- CENTROMEA text — anti-centromere; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N= -, +-
- DNA text — anti-DNA; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 8
- DNA-II integer — anti-DNA; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 8

- id integer — the unique identifier of the gender

- client_id integer — the unique number
- gender text; values: F：female M：male

- A13 real — unemployment rate 1996

- A15 integer — no. of committed crimes 1995
- A16 integer — no. of committed crimes 1996

- account_id integer — the id number identifying the account

- amount integer — approved amount; values: unit：US dollar

- payments real — monthly payments; values: unit：month
- status text — repayment status; values: 'A' stands for contract finished, no problems;'B' stands for contract finished, loan not paid;'C' stands for running contract, OK so far;'D' stands for running contract, client in debt

## account

- disp_id integer — disposition id

- client_id integer — the unique number
- gender text; values: F：female M：male

- disp_id integer — unique number of identifying this row of record
- client_id integer — id number of client
- account_id integer — id number of account
- type text — type of disposition; values: "OWNER" : "USER" : "DISPONENT"commonsense evidence:the account can only have the right to issue permanent orders or apply for loans

- A3 text — region
- A4 text
- A5 text — municipality < district < region
- A6 text — municipality < district < region
- A7 text — municipality < district < region
- A8 integer — municipality < district < region
- A9 integer; values: not useful

- A13 real — unemployment rate 1996

forge.sql:
WITH eligible_events AS (
  SELECT attendance.link_to_event AS event_id
  FROM attendance
  GROUP BY attendance.link_to_event
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS meeting_count
FROM event
INNER JOIN eligible_events ON event.event_id = eligible_events.event_id
WHERE event.type = 'Meeting'

forge.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT budget.amount
  FROM budget
  INNER JOIN event ON budget.link_to_event = event.event_id
  WHERE budget.category = 'Advertisement' AND event.event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff'
),
october AS (
  SELECT budget.amount
  FROM budget
  INNER JOIN event ON budget.link_to_event = event.event_id
  WHERE budget.category = 'Advertisement' AND event.event_name = 'October Meeting'
)
SELECT yearly.yearly_amount / october.october_amount AS times
FROM yearly
CROSS JOIN october

forge.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT races.raceId) AS times_held, circuits.location, circuits.lat, circuits.lng
FROM circuits
INNER JOIN races ON circuits.circuitId = races.circuitId
WHERE circuits.country = 'Austria'
GROUP BY circuits.location, circuits.lat, circuits.lng

INNER JOIN atom ON connected.atom_id = atom.atom_id

INNER JOIN connected ON bond.bond_id = connected.bond_id

forge.sql:
WITH local_diff AS (
  SELECT schools.School AS school_name, schools.DOCType AS doc_type, frpm."Enrollment (K-12)" - frpm."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" AS difference
  FROM schools
  INNER JOIN frpm ON schools.CDSCode = frpm.CDSCode
  WHERE schools.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
)
SELECT school_name, doc_type
FROM local_diff
WHERE difference > (
  SELECT average_difference_value
  FROM local_diff
)

SELECT s.School, s.DOCType
FROM schools AS s
JOIN frpm AS f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
WHERE s.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
  AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > (
    SELECT AVG(f2."Enrollment (K-12)" - f2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)")
    FROM schools AS s2
    JOIN frpm AS f2 ON s2.CDSCode = f2.CDSCode
    WHERE s2.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
  );

WITH youngest AS (
  SELECT MAX(client.birth_date) AS max_birth_date
  FROM client
),
highest_salary AS (
  SELECT MAX(district.A11) AS max_salary
  FROM district
)
SELECT DISTINCT account.account_id
FROM client
INNER JOIN disp ON client.client_id = disp.client_id
INNER JOIN account ON disp.account_id = account.account_id
INNER JOIN district ON client.district_id = district.district_id
INNER JOIN youngest ON client.birth_date = youngest.max_birth_date
INNER JOIN highest_salary ON district.A11 = highest_salary.max_salary

SELECT district.A2, ((district.A13 - district.A12) / district.A12) * 100 AS unemployment_rate_increment_percentage
FROM loan
INNER JOIN account ON loan.account_id = account.account_id
INNER JOIN district ON account.district_id = district.district_id
WHERE loan.status = 'D'

assistant.text:
SELECT d.A2, ((d.A13 - d.A12) / d.A12) * 100
FROM district AS d
JOIN account AS a ON a.district_id = d.district_id
JOIN loan AS l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE l.status = 'D';

forge.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS loan_count
FROM loan
INNER JOIN account ON loan.account_id = account.account_id
WHERE loan.date BETWEEN '950101' AND '971231' AND loan.amount >= 250000 AND account.frequency = 'POPLATEK MESICNE'

assistant.text:
SELECT a.account_id, COUNT(l.loan_id) AS loan_count
FROM account AS a
JOIN loan AS l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE a.frequency = 'POPLATEK MESICNE'
  AND l.amount >= 250000
  AND l.date BETWEEN '950101' AND '971231'
GROUP BY a.account_id;
